dispositions.method: Round two took the ten candidates that round one read but did not admit (each counted by the item finder in 7 or 8 newspapers), leaving out the reports of Cherokee and Creek plans, which need careful framing first. Each candidate's printings were looked for with phrase searches over all 2,319 pages of 1776 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns_round2.json, phrase_hits_round2.json), and every hit was read. Papers with pages in a story's weeks but no printing were searched by hand for garbled printings; none was found. Nine stories were admitted (15 groups, 87 printings); one candidate was not.
dispositions.selection_rule: As in round one, a story is admitted when it reaches 7 or more newspapers, and printings are counted item by item. Where a candidate turned out to be two related printed items, each item is its own group under a parent story, as in round one; in this round such a sub-story can reach fewer than 7 papers (the Commons committee report on the Prohibitory bill, 6; the settled clause, 5; the Howes' declaration of 19 September, 6). A paper that printed an item again later counts each printing.

candidates_split.The Commons debate on the Prohibitory bi: two London reports joined by the clause on captures: the committee debate of 5 December 1775 with the clause printed with blanks for its dates (6 papers), and the clause as settled on 8 December (5 papers). Admitted as two groups under a parent story.
candidates_split.Governor Penn examined in the Lords: two London items: a short report that Penn was examined (7 papers) and the long account of the examination with questions and answers (8 papers). Admitted as two groups under a parent story.
candidates_split.Congress on refusing Continental bills (: Congress's resolution of 11 January 1776 (7 papers) is admitted. The other printings are not one notice repeated: they are separate notices of committees of inspection, which quote the resolution and then name people found to have refused the bills (see not_admitted).
candidates_split.The Howe brothers' declarations (item fi: several documents with the same heading: Lord Howe's declaration of June 1776 published by Congress in July (7 papers) and the brothers' declaration of 19 September (6 papers) are admitted as two groups under a parent story; the rest are listed in not_admitted.

added_by_phrase_search: PEP 1776-01-13 p1 to VGb 02-02 p2: the 11 January resolution itself, which the item finder had joined to the committee notices
VGb 1776-03-29 p2: a one-sentence notice of the fast of 17 May (condensed report)
NYP 1776-05-02 p3: a shorter, reworded report of the sloop Liberty's capture (condensed report)

not_admitted.Deserters from the Cork regiments (PG 01: a one-sentence London paragraph in 5 papers, below the round's 7. The item finder's 8 papers came from the neighbouring London paragraphs. The New-York Gazette of 5 February prints a different report of desertions at Cork.
not_admitted.Committee of inspection notices under th: separate notices of the Philadelphia committee of inspection and observation (dated 5 and 20 February, 26 March and 9 April) and one Gloucester County committee notice, each quoting the resolution and then publishing the names of people the committee had found to have refused the bills. They are different documents, so they were not added to the resolution's group. Whether to show them, and how, given that they name private persons, is a decision for later.
not_admitted.Another London report on the Prohibitory: the bill's second reading of 1 December 1775, on a different clause; 3 papers.
not_admitted.The Synod's notice on the fast (NYG 04-2: the Synod of New-York and Philadelphia moves its meeting because Congress's fast falls in its session; a different document.
not_admitted.Fasts of August 1776 (Massachusetts, 1 A: other fast days, not Congress's of 17 May.
not_admitted.A Philadelphia letter of 11 April on the: a different report of the same capture; 1 paper.
not_admitted.The Howes' joint declaration of 14 July: printed in the New-York Gazette only, next to the declaration of 19 September; its text is that of Lord Howe's June declaration in the July group.
not_admitted.A parody of the September declaration (P: 'the King's Commissioners for deluding the good people of America': a satirical rewriting, printed after the declaration in the Pennsylvania Gazette ('EXPLANATION of the above') and on its own in three papers. Commentary, not the declaration; 4 papers.
not_admitted.The London notice of the Howes' commissi: a different document (letters patent of 3 May naming the commissioners); 6 papers.
